title: Same Tree
statement: Given the roots of two binary trees `p` and `q`, return `True` if they are the same: identical shape, and equal values in every position.

example.why: The right children differ: 3 in one tree, 4 in the other.

idea: Two trees are the same when their roots match, their left subtrees are the same, **and** their right subtrees are the same.
That definition is recursive, so the code is too: compare one pair of nodes, then recurse into both pairs of children.
Two base cases stop it: both spots empty → equal; exactly one empty, or different values → not equal.

complexity.timeWhy: Each pair of nodes is compared once (n = size of the smaller tree).
complexity.spaceWhy: The recursion stack is as deep as the tree's height h.

steps.text: Our example: **`p = [1,2,3], q = [1,2,4]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`p` holds 1 and `q` holds 1: these match. Now their left subtrees must match **and** their right subtrees must match.
`p` holds 2 and `q` holds 2: these match. Now their left subtrees must match **and** their right subtrees must match.
Both spots are empty, so they match: return True. (Every pair of empty spots ends this way.)
Below the pair of 2s: both sides matched, so return **True**.
`p` holds 3 but `q` holds 4. The values differ → **different**.
Below the pair of 1s: not everything matched, so return **False**.
Done — the answer is **`False`**. The right children differ: 3 in one tree, 4 in the other.
